summary: The Cincinnati Bengals beat the Buffalo Bills 24-18 on NBC's "Sunday Night Football" on Nov. 5, 2023, at Paycor Stadium, winning their fourth straight after a 1-3 start. Joe Burrow outplayed Josh Allen while Lou Anarumo's defense held Buffalo to 11 points after the Bengals built a 21-7 halftime lead. The note is a live-blog of drives and scoring plays, plus pregame notes and viewing information.
one_line: Bengals beat the Bills 24-18 on Sunday Night Football, their fourth straight win, behind Joe Burrow's 348 yards and a strong defensive second half.
key_facts: The Bengals beat the Bills 24-18 on Sunday Night Football (Nov. 5, 2023) at Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, their fourth straight win.
Cincinnati started the season 1-3, including losses to the Browns and Titans in which they scored just three points each.
Quarter scores: Bills 7-0-3-8 (18) and Bengals 14-7-0-3 (24); the Bengals led 21-7 at halftime.
Joe Burrow completed 31-of-44 passes for 348 yards with two touchdowns.
Josh Allen went 26-for-38 for 258 yards, one passing touchdown and an interception, and rushed eight times for 44 yards and a score.
Irv Smith Jr. caught a 7-yard touchdown over Jordan Poyer for the opening score; Joe Mixon added a 2-yard touchdown run, and Drew Sample scored on a short catch-and-run.
Cam Taylor-Britt intercepted Allen for his third interception of the season (Allen's ninth).
Allen hit Stefon Diggs for a 17-yard touchdown and a two-point conversion to make it 24-18 with 3:32 left.
Burrow then threw a 32-yard pass to Tyler Boyd and Mixon ran for the first down so Burrow could kneel out the game.
With the win, the Bengals moved into the final wild-card spot behind the Steelers and Browns, while the Bills fell out of the AFC playoff picture.
Damar Hamlin was inactive but worked out on the field at Paycor Stadium before the game.
NBC has carried Sunday Night Football since 2006 through at least 2033; Mike Tirico, Cris Collinsworth and Melissa Stark were the broadcast crew.
